Harmony Heart Pro (NVC Edition)

A communication coach for couples. You give it the sentence that started the argument; it returns the psychology underneath it, then the same sentence rebuilt as observation, feeling, need and a request you can actually say out loud.

Open the app → ← All projects

Overview

Arguments between partners rarely fail because of the topic. They fail because each person is defending a position instead of naming what they need. Harmony Heart Pro is built to interrupt that loop: it takes the raw thing that was said and re-frames it in Non-Violent Communication form, then helps the other person respond in the same language.

The app is deliberately structured rather than chatty. You set who you are and who your spouse is, choose how assertive the reply should be — Gentle, Balanced or Assertive — and give it the sentence. What comes back is a fixed shape every time: the psychological perspective first, then observation, feeling and need, then a request you can read out, closed with body-language and tone notes.

Two modes cover both directions. They Said… interprets what you just heard; I Said… checks what you are about to say before you say it. It runs in five languages — English, German, French, Spanish and Arabic — in light or dark theme, and it states its own limits in-product: a de-escalation training consultant, not a replacement for a licensed therapist.

How it works

  1. They said. Type or dictate the sentence — or tap one of the built-in examples that couples actually say.
  2. The perspective. A psychological read of the statement: protest behaviour, anxious attachment, an amygdala hijack behind a word like "always".
  3. Observation. The same sentence restated without judgement or interpretation.
  4. Feeling. What your spouse is likely feeling, and the fear sitting underneath it.
  5. Need. The universal human need behind the feeling — to be seen, prioritised, reassured.
  6. The request. A first-person script to say back, followed by how to stand, breathe and sound while saying it.

What's inside

  • A fixed NVC structure instead of open-ended chat — the structure is the product.
  • Identity-aware framing: who you are and who your spouse is changes the wording, not just the pronouns.
  • Three response tones, so the same advice can be gentle or direct depending on the moment.
  • They Said… and I Said… modes for interpreting and for rehearsing.
  • Voice input, so a difficult sentence does not have to be typed.
  • Copy-ready request cards, with body language and tone guidance attached.
  • Five languages and a light or dark theme that follows the room you are in.
  • Native Android delivery through a Capacitor shell, with accounts and history on Supabase.
